body.statement: Under the compatibility regime in the Gaussian-witness definition and whenever \(\sqrt n\geq2\bar H\), uniformly over \(h\in[0,\bar H]\), \[(3-\sqrt5)/2\leq\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma(a_{n,h}))\leq\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma(a_{n,h}))\leq(3+\sqrt5)/2,\] \(E_{P_{n,h}}[\|W_i\|_2^8]\leq1920\{(3+\sqrt5)/2\}^4\), and \(\sigma_{P_{n,h}}(\theta)^2=4(\theta^2+a_{n,h}^2)(1+\theta^2)\in[2,100]\) for every \(\theta\in[-2,2]\). Moreover, \(\beta=(1,0)^{\prime}\), \(\alpha=(0,a_{n,h})^{\prime}\), \(\theta_0=\check\theta=0\), \(\gamma=(0,a_{n,h})^{\prime}\), and \(\delta(P_{n,h})=h/\sqrt n\leq C_{\delta}/\sqrt n\). The raw endpoints are therefore defined and \(\Theta_I(P_{n,h})=[-\sqrt{h/\sqrt n},\sqrt{h/\sqrt n}]\subset(-2,2)\), so \(\operatorname{dist}(\Theta_I(P_{n,h}),\partial K)=2-\sqrt{h/\sqrt n}\geq2-1/\sqrt2>1\); no \(K\)-truncation occurs. Hence \(P_{n,h}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})\) along the full path. The experiment \(\{P_{n,h}:h\in[0,\bar H]\}\) is locally asymptotically normal and mutually contiguous on compact \(h\)-sets.
body.justification: The explicit numerical bounds certify that the entire local path satisfies positive definiteness, fixed relevance, score nondegeneracy, moment control, and parameter-space interiority.
body.gap: Watson et al.'s simulations stay away from equality and do not provide a LAN path through their feasibility boundary.
body.consumer: The path supplies both the exact early kill test and the local-minimax converse experiment.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(h\in[0,\bar H]\), put \(a=a_{n,h}\), and use the specialization \(d=2\), \(\tau=1\), and \(K=[-2,2]\) from \(\mathrm{def:gaussian\mbox{-}witness}\).  Permuting coordinates from \((Z_1,Z_2,X,Y)\) to \((Z_1,X,Z_2,Y)\) turns \(\Sigma(a)\) into the block diagonal matrix
\[
 B_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B_2(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\a&1+a^2\end{pmatrix}. \tag{1}
\]
Both determinants equal one.  The trace of \(B_1\) is three, while the trace of \(B_2(a)\) is \(2+a^2\leq3\).  For a positive \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix of determinant one, the larger eigenvalue is increasing in its trace and the smaller one is its reciprocal.  The eigenvalues of \(B_1\) are \((3\pm\sqrt5)/2\).  Thus (1) proves
\[
 \frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}\leq\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(a)\}
 \leq\lambda_{\max}\{\Sigma(a)\}\leq\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}. \tag{2}
\]
In particular \(\Sigma(a)\) is positive definite.  If \(G_4\sim N(0,I_4)\) and \(L=(3+\sqrt5)/2\), then \(W\) has the same law as \(\Sigma(a)^{1/2}G_4\), whence \(\|W\|_2^8\leq L^4\|G_4\|_2^8\).  Since \(\|G_4\|_2^2\) is chi-squared with four degrees of freedom,
\[
 E\|G_4\|_2^8=4\cdot6\cdot8\cdot10=1920,
\]
which gives the asserted eighth-moment bound.

The observable covariance blocks are \(\Sigma_{zz}=I_2\), \(\Sigma_{zx}=(1,0)^{\prime}\), and \(\Sigma_{zy}=(0,a)^{\prime}\).  Therefore
\[
 \beta=(1,0)^{\prime},\qquad
 \alpha=(0,a)^{\prime},\qquad
 \check\theta=0,
\]
and the structural representation in \(P_{n,h}\) has \(\theta_0=0\) and \(\gamma=(0,a)^{\prime}\).  Its leakage norm is \(a\leq1=\tau\), its relevance norm is one, and
\[
 \lambda(P_{n,h})=a^2,
 \qquad
 \delta(P_{n,h})=1-a^2=\frac{h}{\sqrt n}\leq\frac{C_\delta}{\sqrt n}. \tag{3}
\]
We next calculate the score variance rather than assuming it.  At this law, differentiation of the two least-squares reduced forms gives
\[
 d\alpha=Z\{Y-\alpha^{\prime}Z\}=Z\epsilon_y,
 \qquad
 d\beta=Z\{X-\beta^{\prime}Z\}=Z\epsilon_x.
\]
For \(g_\theta=\alpha-\theta\beta=(-\theta,a)^{\prime}\), differentiation of \(q_P(\theta)=\|g_\theta\|_2^2-1\) consequently yields the influence function
\[
 \psi_{P_{n,h}}(W;\theta)
 =2(-\theta Z_1+aZ_2)(\epsilon_y-\theta\epsilon_x). \tag{4}
\]
The two factors in (4) are independent centered Gaussian variables, with variances \(\theta^2+a^2\) and \(1+\theta^2\), respectively.  Hence
\[
 \sigma_{P_{n,h}}(\theta)^2
 =4(\theta^2+a^2)(1+\theta^2). \tag{5}
\]
The condition \(\sqrt n\geq2\bar H\) gives \(a^2=1-h/\sqrt n\geq1/2\).  For \(\theta\in[-2,2]\), (5) is therefore between \(2\) and \(4(4+1)(1+4)=100\).  Equations (2)--(5), together with the numerical compatibility inequalities in the witness definition, verify every covariance, moment, relevance, leakage, and score-nondegeneracy condition in \(\mathcal P_W\).

By the endpoint-domain lemma and (3),
\[
 \Theta_I(P_{n,h})=
 \left[-\sqrt{h/\sqrt n},\sqrt{h/\sqrt n}\right]. \tag{6}
\]
Moreover, \(h/\sqrt n\leq1/2\), so its distance from the boundary of \([-2,2]\) is
\[
 2-\sqrt{h/\sqrt n}\geq2-1/\sqrt2>1\geq m_K. \tag{7}
\]
Thus the parameter margin holds, no \(K\)-truncation occurs, and (3) proves \(P_{n,h}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_\delta)\), uniformly in \(h\).

It remains to verify the experiment claim.  Under the reference \(P_{n,0}\), only the conditional regression of \(Y\) on \(Z_2\) changes.  With \(u_{n,h}=\sqrt n(a_{n,h}-1)\), its log likelihood ratio is exactly
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{n,h}^{\,n}}{dP_{n,0}^{\,n}}
 =u_{n,h}\Delta_n-\frac{u_{n,h}^2}{2}\,n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_{2i}^2,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_{2i}\epsilon_{y,i}. \tag{8}
\]
Uniformly on the compact \(h\)-set, \(u_{n,h}=-h/2+O(n^{-1/2})\).  A Taylor expansion of the characteristic function of the centered summands \(Z_{2i}\epsilon_{y,i}\), whose variance is one and whose third absolute moment is finite, gives \(\Delta_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\); the same moment calculation gives \(n^{-1}\sum Z_{2i}^2\to1\) in probability.  Substitution in (8) yields
\[
 \log\frac{dP_{n,h}^{\,n}}{dP_{n,0}^{\,n}}
 =-\frac h2\Delta_n-\frac{h^2}{8}+o_{P_{n,0}}(1), \tag{9}
\]
uniformly for \(h\in[0,\bar H]\).  This is the LAN expansion with local coordinate \(-h/2\).

For completeness, contiguity follows directly.  If \(\Delta a=a_{n,h}-1\), conditioning on the \(Z_{2i}\)'s in (8) gives
\[
 E_{P_{n,0}}\left[\left(\frac{dP_{n,h}^{\,n}}{dP_{n,0}^{\,n}}\right)^2\right]
 =(1-2\Delta a^2)^{-n/2}, \tag{10}
\]
which is uniformly bounded on compact \(h\)-sets because \(n\Delta a^2\to h^2/4\).  The analogous reverse likelihood ratio has the same bound.  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to either likelihood ratio shows that an event whose probability tends to zero under one sequence has probability tending to zero under the other.  This proves mutual contiguity and completes the proof.
